items.title: Google Erases a Record $500 Billion as AI Eats Into Sales
items.summary: Alphabet's shares fell more than 13% on October 29, erasing over $500 billion in market value in the stock's biggest one-day plunge ever. The drop followed disappointing search and advertising revenue that reinforced investor fears that AI products are cutting into Google's core search business, even as the company maintained its spending guidance for the year.
items.why_it_matters: The reaction shows Wall Street is no longer giving AI spenders a free pass -- even strong cloud growth isn't enough if AI appears to threaten a company's existing cash-cow business.

items.title: Two fears will decide the fate of Anthropic's giant IPO
items.summary: Investors weighing Anthropic's blockbuster IPO must balance missing out on extraordinary AI growth against risks including potentially 'existential' dangers from the technology, according to the Financial Times. Other coverage of Anthropic's S-1 filing has questioned its revenue and compute costs, and credit-rating agencies are reportedly expected to give the company only a high 'junk' rating once it goes public.
items.why_it_matters: Anthropic's IPO is shaping up as a referendum on whether Wall Street will keep funding the AI buildout at today's prices, or start demanding proof it pays off.

items.title: Mistral releases weights for its trillion-parameter AI model, targeting cybersecurity
items.summary: French AI lab Mistral released the open weights of Mistral Large 4, a trillion-parameter model it says gives organizations more control over their cyber defenses than closed models can. Coverage of the release, nicknamed 'Le Chonk,' says it matches or outperforms top Chinese open-weight models like DeepSeek and Z.ai on coding and cybersecurity benchmarks.
items.why_it_matters: A trillion-parameter model released as open weights raises the bar for what's available outside the closed frontier labs, and strengthens a European challenger to Chinese open-weight models.

items.title: Making it easier for websites to express AI training preferences
items.summary: OpenAI, along with Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic, will adopt a shared robots.txt-based signal that lets website operators communicate their AI training preferences once instead of setting them separately for each company. OpenAI says it will honor this shared 'policy token' signal from participating providers.
items.why_it_matters: A common opt-out standard backed by the biggest AI labs could finally give publishers one lever to control AI training use across the industry, instead of fighting each company separately.

items.title: How we detect frontier model misalignment
items.summary: OpenAI described the layered monitoring systems it uses to detect misalignment and unauthorized behavior in its frontier models and AI agents, aiming to let human responders intervene before incidents escalate.
items.why_it_matters: As AI agents get more autonomy, how well labs can actually catch misbehavior in real time becomes a key test of whether current safety approaches scale.

items.title: Canada, Nvidia Back Cohere at Over $20 Billion Valuation
items.summary: Cohere is raising a funding round that values the Canadian AI model maker at over $20.5 billion, roughly tripling its valuation from a year ago, with commitments from Nvidia, the Canadian government, Germany's Schwarz Group, and telecom firm BCE. The Wall Street Journal reports Canada will take an equity stake in Cohere as part of the deal.
items.why_it_matters: A national government taking a direct equity stake in an AI lab shows how seriously some countries now treat domestic AI champions as strategic assets, not just companies to regulate.

items.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
items.summary: Anthropic's official Claude Code extension on the Cursor Marketplace was compromised with a backdoor for nearly 12 hours before it was caught. It's still unknown how the attackers gained access to Anthropic's verified Cursor publisher account.
items.why_it_matters: A widely trusted AI coding tool getting silently backdoored through a verified publisher account is a reminder that the AI coding supply chain is now a real attack surface.

items.title: Google's satellite AI server transmits its first response to Earth
items.summary: Google successfully booted up the Tensor Processing Units aboard its AI-equipped satellite, part of its Project Suncatcher effort, and had the onboard Gemma 4 model generate its first response from orbit: a haiku about being in space. It's the first time Google has run a frontier-style model on a TPU in orbit.
items.why_it_matters: Running AI chips in orbit is still an early experiment, but it signals that space-based computing is moving from theory toward a real engineering roadmap for AI infrastructure.

items.title: [AINews] Gemini 4 Carbon tops leaderboards, launches for cyber defenders
items.summary: Google's new Gemini 4 Carbon model is leading independent evaluation leaderboards, according to Latent Space's AI News roundup. Initial access is being limited to trusted cyber defenders rather than opened broadly.
items.why_it_matters: A new leaderboard-topping frontier model matters on its own, but gating early access to cybersecurity defenders also signals labs are increasingly wary of releasing their most capable systems broadly.

items.title: Microsoft $25 Billion Blowout Bond Puts It in AI Winners' Circle
items.summary: Microsoft raised at least $25 billion in its first US investment-grade bond offering in nearly a decade, with investors giving the sale a strong reception, to help fund its AI infrastructure buildout. The move comes even as Microsoft's profit jumped 32% last quarter despite $45.2 billion in capital spending, keeping free cash flow positive unlike Meta, Alphabet and Amazon.
items.why_it_matters: Microsoft tapping the bond market, while still posting the strongest cash flow among its Big Tech AI-spending peers, underscores how differently investors are now pricing each hyperscaler's AI bet.
